sections.h2: Where is McMinnville and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
McMinnville is the county seat and largest city of Yamhill County, in the Willamette Valley at the foot of the Oregon Coast Range. It sits where the North and South forks of the Yamhill River meet, about 37 miles southwest of Portland and 26 miles northwest of Salem, at 161 feet above sea level.

The city covers 10.58 square miles, all of it land. Downtown runs along East Third Street, the older residential streets spread west along West Second Street, and collector roads such as Baker Creek Road and Cypress Street tie the outer residential and industrial areas together. A house on the west side and one near the highway corridor can sell to very different buyers, so the street matters as much as the city name.

sections.h2: How did McMinnville grow into a city of about 34,000?
sections.html:
McMinnville began with a land claim. William T. Newby claimed the site in 1844, built a grist mill in 1853, and platted the town on May 5, 1856, naming it for his hometown of McMinnville, Tennessee. The plat was not recorded until July 1865.

The town incorporated in 1876 and became a city in 1882. Voters moved the county seat here from Lafayette in 1886, which is why county offices and courts are in town today.

sections.h2: What jobs and industries support McMinnville homeowners?
sections.html:
Health care, higher education and manufacturing anchor the local job base. The 2020 list of top employers named Willamette Valley Medical Center, Linfield University and Cascade Steel Rolling Mills.

  • Linfield University opened in 1858 as the Baptist College of McMinnville, took its current name in 2020, and enrolls about 2,000 students on nearly 200 acres.
  • Cascade Steel makes finished steel from recycled scrap and is a subsidiary of Radius Recycling.
  • Oregon Mutual Insurance dates to 1894, and First Federal Savings and Loan was founded here in 1922.
  • Organic Valley bought the Farmers Cooperative Creamery in 2016. A 2021 fire destroyed the plant, and it was rebuilt and reopened.

Wine adds another layer. The McMinnville AVA was established in January 2005 and covers 14 wineries and 523 acres within the Willamette Valley AVA. Yamhill County has the largest vineyard area of any Oregon county. A seller whose house sits near vineyard land or the downtown tasting rooms is selling into that setting.

sections.h2: What does McMinnville's climate mean for an older house?
sections.html:
McMinnville has a warm-summer Mediterranean climate, so the main wear on a house comes from a long wet season. Monthly mean temperatures run from 40.5 degrees in December to 67.5 degrees in August, and rain averages 37.64 inches a year with November the wettest month.

The extremes are real but rare. The record high is 114 degrees, set June 28, 2021, and the record low is minus 7 degrees on January 31, 1950. Marine fog from the coast is common. Roofs, gutters, siding and crawl spaces take the brunt of months of damp, so those are worth a look before a buyer does.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and the airport shape McMinnville real estate?
sections.html:
Oregon Route 99W runs through the city, Oregon Route 18 bypasses it to the south and leads to the coast, and Route 47 begins just northeast of the city limits. Newberg and Portland are reachable along 99W, which matters for sellers whose buyers commute.

  • McMinnville Municipal Airport is city-owned, and the Oregon International Air Show has been held there each September since 2019.
  • The Portland & Western Railroad has served the city since 1993 on a line leased from Union Pacific.
  • Yamhill County Transit Area runs public transit.
  • The Evergreen Aviation & Space Museum, home of the Spruce Goose, is reached from the same Route 18 corridor as the airport.

sections.h2: Who provides power, water and sewer in McMinnville?
sections.html:
McMinnville Water and Light, a city-owned utility, handles electric and water service. Its main office is at 340 NE Kirby Street, and the phone number is (503) 472-6158.

The utility reports an electric territory of 75 square miles and 162 miles of water main. Residential sewer charges are based on water use from November through March. A seller moving out should call the office to set a final meter reading and a date to transfer service, since the utility's site does not spell out the steps for a sale.

sections.h2: What are McMinnville's schools and colleges?
sections.html:
The McMinnville School District serves about 7,000 students in kindergarten through grade 12. It runs five elementary schools, two middle schools and McMinnville High School, which has more than 2,000 students. Private options include McMinnville Montessori School, McMinnville Christian Academy and St. James Catholic Elementary School.

Chemeketa Community College has had a Yamhill Valley campus here with accreditation since 2011. Check attendance boundaries with the district before you describe a house as being in a particular school area.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due on a McMinnville house?
sections.html:
Oregon bills property tax in three installments, due November 15, February 15 and May 15. Yamhill County, where McMinnville sits, collects the bill.

  • Paying everything by November 15 earns a 3% discount, and paying two-thirds by then earns 2%.
  • Late amounts accrue interest of 1 1/3% per month, starting after December 15 for the first installment.
  • Under ORS 308.146, taxable value generally grows no faster than 3% a year unless the property changes, so a buyer's bill can differ from the seller's.

Ask the title company to prorate the current year's tax at closing.

sections.h2: What must a McMinnville seller disclose?
sections.html:
Most Oregon sellers of one-to-four-unit homes must give each buyer who makes a written offer a signed seller's property disclosure statement. A buyer who receives it can revoke the offer within five business days unless a written waiver was already delivered.

Some sales are excluded under ORS 105.470, including sales by court-appointed personal representatives and trustees and sales by a financial institution that took the property through foreclosure. If you are selling an inherited house, ask the estate's attorney whether the exclusion applies.

sections.h2: What sellers in McMinnville usually weigh
sections.html:
Sellers here usually compare three routes: listing with an agent, selling without one, or accepting an as-is offer from a cash buyer. A cash buyer sets its own terms and timeline, so compare more than the headline number.

  • Condition: wet-season roof, gutter and crawl-space wear is common in older houses.
  • Timing: tax installments, utility transfer and any move-out date.
  • Paperwork: the disclosure statement, or the estate exclusion if it applies.
  • Costs: who pays for repairs, title and closing.

faqs.q: How many people live in McMinnville?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 34,647 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 34,319.
Yamhill County. McMinnville is its county seat and its largest city, so the assessor and tax office serving your house are the county's.

faqs.q: When are Oregon property taxes due?
faqs.a: The three installments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15. A 3% discount applies if you pay in full by November 15.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a disclosure statement when I sell in McMinnville?
faqs.a: Usually yes for a one-to-four-unit home, with exclusions such as court-appointed sellers and foreclosing financial institutions. A buyer who gets the statement has five business days to revoke the offer unless they waived that right.

faqs.q: Who do I call to stop utilities when I sell?
faqs.a: Call McMinnville Water and Light at (503) 472-6158 to schedule a final reading and transfer of service.

faqs.q: Can I sell a McMinnville house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers, including cash buyers, take houses in any condition, but expect the offer to reflect the repairs. Get more than one opinion of the work needed.
